case_name: Raju Pandurang Mahale v State of Maharashtra and Another
respondent:
State of Maharashtra and Another
Supreme Court of India

11 February 2004
Appeal (Cr.) 616 of 2003
The Judgment was delivered by: Arijit Pasayat, J.
1. Appellant calls in question legality of the conviction recorded in terms of Ss. 342 and 354 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short 'the IPC') by the Trial Court, and affirmed in appeal by the impugned judgment by learned Single Judge of the Bombay High Court, Aurangabad Bench. Two appeals were disposed of by a common judgment. Criminal Appeal no. 3 of 98 was filed by the present appellant along with one Pankaj, while the connected Criminal Appeal no. 50/98 was filed by Raju @ Rajesh S. Kopekar.
2. Four accused persons faced trial. The appellants before the High Court were present appellant Raju Pandurang Mahale (A-1), Gautam (A-2), Pankaj (A-3) and Rajesh S. Kopekar (A-4). A-1 to A-4 were convicted for offences punishable u/ss. 376 (2) (g) IPC and each of A-1, A-3 and A-4 was sentenced to suffer
facts: Appellant calls in question legality of the conviction recorded in terms of Ss. 342 and 354 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short 'the IPC') by the Trial Court, and affirmed in appeal by the impugned judgment by learned Single Judge of the Bombay High Court, Aurangabad Bench.
The alleged occurrence took place on 12th and 13th January, 1996. Husband of the prosecutrix (PW-5), at the relevant time, was undergoing imprisonment for life after his conviction in a murder case.
Appellant Raju Pandurang Mahale came to the house of the prosecutrix and told her that Raju @ Rajesh S. Kopekar (accused no. 4) had gone for night duty, and that his wife was alone at home.
The prosecutrix went to her sister's house and narrated incident to her sister (PW-6). Thereafter, they went to the police station and lodged the report.
Investigation was undertaken and charge sheet filed.
issues: Whether the offences u/s. 342 and S. 354 IPC were made out?
Whether the role attributed to the appellant establishes existence of ingredients necessary to constitute offence punishable under Ss. 342 and 354 IPC?
petitioner_arguments: The offences u/s. 342 and S. 354 IPC were not made out.
The role attributed to the appellant does not in any manner establish existence of ingredients necessary to constitute offence punishable under Ss. 342 and 354 IPC.
respondent_arguments: Evidence has been analysed by both the Trial Court and the High Court in great detail.

The role attributed to the appellant by the victim is very clear and in any event S. 34 was pressed into service to show that he shared the common intention regarding commission of the alleged offences.
court_reasoning: The essential ingredients of the offence 'wrongful confinement' are that the accused should have wrongfully confined the complainant and such restraint was to prevent the complainant from proceeding beyond certain circumscribed limits beyond which he/she has a right to proceed.
What constitutes an outrage to female modesty is nowhere defined. The essence of a woman's modesty is her sex.
Modesty in this Section is an attribute associated with female human beings as a class.
holding: The conviction and the sentence as awarded do not need any interference.
The factual scenario clearly establishes commission by the appellant as well of the offence punishable u/s. 342 IPC.
